entities.name: Integrity Protection
entities.description: Mandatory protection mechanism for NAS messages once valid EPS security context exists and secure exchange is established. Responsible for ensuring message authenticity and integrity.

entities.name: Null Integrity Protection Algorithm EIA0
entities.description: Integrity protection algorithm that provides no actual cryptographic protection. Only allowed for unauthenticated UEs requiring emergency services or RLOS access.

entities.name: NAS Signalling Message
entities.description: Non-Access Stratum message exchanged between UE and network. Subject to integrity protection and ciphering requirements.

entities.name: EPS Security Context
entities.description: Security context established between UE and network that includes integrity and ciphering algorithms and keys.

entities.name: Security Header
entities.description: Header field in NAS messages indicating security processing applied, including integrity protection status.

entities.name: MAC Calculation
entities.description: Process of computing Message Authentication Code for integrity protection using NAS message content and sequence number.

entities.name: NAS Sequence Number
entities.description: Sequence number included in NAS messages used as input for MAC calculation during integrity protection.

entities.name: Emergency Bearer Services Access
entities.description: Condition where UE is unauthenticated but allowed to establish emergency services or access RLOS.

relations.description: Integrity protection becomes mandatory once valid EPS security context exists and is taken into use.
Null integrity protection algorithm EIA0 is only allowed for unauthenticated UEs requiring emergency services.
NAS messages contain security header indicating integrity protection status.
Integrity protection is implemented through MAC calculation using NAS message and sequence number.
MAC calculation includes NAS sequence number as input parameter.
When null integrity algorithm EIA0 is used, NAS messages with security header indicating integrity protection are still regarded as integrity protected despite no actual protection.
